status: draft package ownership contract, not built packages
base: Ubuntu26.04 arm64 essential with dpkg and apt

architecture_roles.arm64: native Ubuntu base, systemd/broker/new applications, all kernel modules
architecture_roles.armel: current proprietary ASUS ABI plus source rebuilt for softfp
architecture_roles.armhf: optional independently requested packages; enabled only with corresponding loader/runtime/repository availability

merged_usr.rule: Use exact base-files shape from inspected Ubuntu packages; do not infer /usr/sbin -> bin. Complete collision-checked merge before dpkg payload installation.

core_runtime_packages.custom_glibc: Rebuild distribution packaging for libc6/libc6-dev/libc-bin and required companions; keep cross-architecture libc6 versions exactly matched for Multi-Arch:same. Do not install a second package that force-overwrites official libc6 ownership.
core_runtime_packages.libcrypt: Provide armel libcrypt.so.1 with audited old symbol versions through rebuilt libcrypt1/libxcrypt packaging; stock GLIBC_PRIVATE-dependent libcrypt cannot accompany new glibc unchanged.
core_runtime_packages.tools: Ubuntu-native package paths and GCC specs/sysroot/multiarch search semantics. Target flags apply to rebuilt target code. New/rebuilt code defaults time64; only proven vendor protocol/API boundaries retain explicit old-width compatibility.
core_runtime_packages.package_updates: Signed custom repository for board packages and custom runtimes, with scoped version pinning. Do not disable official security repositories or use trusted=yes. Repository availability for armel must be established independently of Ubuntu arm64/armhf.

proposed_packages.name: asus-be19000ai-vendor-libs
proposed_packages.multi_arch: same only if common files are byte-identical and all payload libraries are architecture-qualified
proposed_packages.notes: Vendor private libraries and plugins retained by exact hashes; reviewed flat compatibility aliases tracked by this package or a separate compatibility package.

proposed_packages.name: asus-be19000ai-apps
owns: ASUS rc/httpd/cfg_client and board-specific armel tools at collision-audited legacy paths
proposed_packages.notes: Keep original executable identity paths until ASUS process-validation source is ported and tested; no generic rc or binary replacement by untracked tar overlay.

proposed_packages.name: asus-be19000ai-native-tools
proposed_packages.notes: Preserve original14 native vendor ELF files only after individual role/ownership audit; never relabel them armel.

proposed_packages.name: asus-be19000ai-webui
proposed_packages.multi_arch: foreign only if dependencies and content actually architecture-independent
proposed_packages.notes: Architecture-dependent CGI executables stay with apps package; device credentials/data are never packaged.

proposed_packages.name: asus-be19000ai-system-integration
proposed_packages.notes: Owns orchestration only; bounded named actions, no implicit reboot in maintainer scripts, no installation-time hardware initialization in a build chroot.

proposed_packages.name: linux-image-be19000ai-leon
owns: versioned kernel/module payload and reproducible metadata
proposed_packages.notes: Vendor4.19 compatible modules stay separate from Ubuntu generic linux-image packages. Installing a .deb stages a candidate; firmware-slot writing remains explicit verified deployment.

proposed_packages.name: asus-be19000ai-platform
proposed_packages.notes: Metapackage pins a tested coherent kernel/userspace/integration release; exact dependencies determined from built packages.

durable_paths./etc: real persistent directory with dpkg conffiles; no tmp/etc symlink
durable_paths./jffs: preserved vendor persistent data with separately audited mount
durable_paths./rom/etc: legacy read-only defaults, never wholesale copied over Ubuntu /etc

ownership_rules: No two packages own divergent content at the same normalized merged-/usr path. Inventory aliases before install; do not use --force-overwrite.
Library-only packages may declare Multi-Arch:same only when coinstallation is structurally valid; executable packages cannot be made coinstallable merely by setting that field.
Use package relationships Breaks/Replaces only for a planned package transition, not to seize Ubuntu base files. Preserve modified conffiles through normal dpkg handling.
ASUS generated runtime configs get explicit path ownership/atomic writes; no stock sysinit truncation of Ubuntu fstab, hosts, resolv.conf, machine-id, apt or dpkg state.
Do not install vendor /bin,/sbin BusyBox links over Ubuntu binaries. Retain private vendor applets where their behavior differs and patch selected callsites only with regression proof.
No package maintainer script writes boot metadata, reformats a partition, restarts radios during offline assembly or commits the active boot slot.
service_ownership: ASUS owns hardware/NVRAM policy initially; systemd owns managed process lifetime. DNS, DHCP and network interfaces must have one manager, not parallel Ubuntu and ASUS daemons.
acceptance: See six acceptance_gates in the audit. This policy is not an assurance of ASUS compatibility or a flashable image.

time64_policy.default: time64 for every new/rebuildable component; ARM32 _TIME_BITS=64,_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64; arm64 native64
time64_policy.legacy: narrow measured retained-blob ABI boundary with fixed-width protocol/API and checked conversions; no global armel downgrade
